title: Todd Monken Press Conference | November 16th, 2026
text: Uh, you know, after the match Deshaun talked about, you know, just entering the tournament and then you have a chance.  Hablaste de estar seis y cuatro.   I'm just curious, do you mention the playoffs with the guys and, if so , at what point do you start talking about them? Absolutely not. I honestly never talk about that with the players, because it has nothing to do with the day we're having, you know, the day when, let's say, the day you ask the question, you know? What matters most is that day, how we prepare for that day.  No, no, I don't discuss that with the players and no... I think it's the wrong approach to take in terms of where we want to be as a team, and it's a day-to-day approach. Understood. And then, when you talk about Harold being captain and having earned that as the season progresses, in what aspects have you seen him grow to take on that leadership role? Bueno, se lo ganó por su diligencia.  He earned it because of the work you put in not only on the practice field, but... what do you do at night?  I mean, are you reviewing the tactics?  I mean, when you get to the building, are you ready to start?   Are you... understanding the developmental aspect of this in terms of you as a player and what it takes to be an elite player? And I think it has made a lot of progress in that regard.   It's not that I was below the standard , but there are certain...it's one thing to be a rookie and not have things expected of you.   It's another thing to take those next steps where expectations increase in everything you do. And he has done a great job over the last month elevating certain aspects of his preparation. Thank you. Ahora pasamos con Tony. Very good. Coach, it seems that Deshaun is playing with more confidence than we 've ever seen from him.   I know you were n't here the previous four years , but we've all seen it. And health was a big issue the previous four years and his health is fine now, but I go back to the exhibition game against Buffalo and it seemed like a turning point this season.   Do you agree with that, and what changed for him? Well, I've said it many times when we met after that, it really was n't about her physical features.   It was really about where you are mentally and emotionally. As I said before, have you gotten rid of this?   So , you've really let him go?   Have you really let go of the frustrations you've been holding onto for the past few years ? But if you haven't done it, you can say so , but only if you really let it go. And if you haven't done it, then it doesn't matter what we do.  It doesn't matter if you're physically healthy, mentally you're not in a good place.  And I felt that our conversation got straight to the point.  Sentí que él lo había dejado ir.   You know, he had vented.   I did n't see anyone who was devastated .  I saw someone who was injured.  There is a difference.  I think he was injured.   I do n't think it was wrecked. And I think that was the first step in terms of, well, where do we go from here? And just like your offense in general, you probably consider him a work in progress in your system. Oh, 100%. Yes, so where will his growth in his game come from now? Well, I think the more we repeat concepts, the better we do in protection .  I believe that the better our young players are at getting into their positions and at understanding the details of their routes and concepts, the more confidence they will have in where to put the ball. I think he's still developing in terms of his steps, the consistency of his steps, his footwork, where he focuses his gaze, and exhausting all his progressions.  Again, what will help with that? Consistency in the concepts, repetition, that we will continue working with him. And he has made an effort. I mean, he's trying to do what we asked him to do, and it's showing. Yes, Todd, how good was Jerry Jeudy's catch on the 65-yard play?  And then the exchange that Deshaun and Jerry had about it, you know, how they talked about working on it in practice and then came back to it on the bench. So I was wondering about Jerry's reception and his development this season. Well, it was something we had seen an opportunity for when analyzing this year's and last year's tapes, in their coverage, that if we could fix the weak side, we could make Jerry cross in front of the deep end. So we worked on it in practice. And you don't always get the training you're looking for, but this time you did.  And they did a great job.  He did a great job opening up space at the back, we did a good job protecting, and Deshaun did a great job throwing the ball.  Jerry showed an extra gear.  I thought the pass was too long, but Jerry showed extra speed to reach it.  So congratulations to those guys and to the protection. Now we move on to Fred.   There was a lot of talk about the run defense, and it didn't start off very well, but overall, I think they allowed 255 yards in the first half and only about 35 in the second. Is that simply due to the pressure on the quarterback, or can you explain how they slowed down both the running and passing attacks?   I think Brown had 21 yards. Well, some of that is true. I think some of that is true regarding the race. Uh, but you rarely watch a game, what was the score? 17 to zero early in the second quarter, is that what happened ?  And 200 yards of offense.  I mean, how many NFL games have you seen that end 70-0 with 800 yards of offense? So, it's not feasible, right?  It's not feasible.  Whether you get 17 points in six or seven sets or in the first three, just play the next play, man.  Play the next series. And if you don't have the drive, you fight to get it back. And when you have the momentum, you maintain it, like I said last night, you know, you keep your foot on the gas, man, and you only go forward when you have it. And momentum is a powerful thing. And then, when you have it in your favor, man, you have to take advantage of it.  And that's what our boys have done and what we didn't do at the start of the game. But I just think the idea that , oh, it started this way and that's why it's going to continue this way... Like I said, look up an NFL game and see if it ended 68 to whatever, zero at the end of the game and they had 800 yards of offense.  That does n't exist.  It's the same in the NBA.  It can be a great first half and not so much the second.  It's a game of making plays, getting stops, scoring points, and regaining momentum. Let's go with Joe. Well, going into a bye week with the first-year staff you have, is it an advantage to get to it after 10 games, compared to if you had the bye early , in terms of doing a self-assessment and all that? It's good to do the self-assessment a little later. I'd prefer it to be a little later, but you do n't know how the season is going to go. A year ago, where I was and in the situation we were in, we needed that week off.  And sometimes, when you're feeling a bit down, you need it at certain times during the season;  Regardless of the self-assessment, you need it to get your team back, right? You need to do certain things to feel good. I think this works wonderfully.   You know, I found out after we won in Tennessee and we were five and two, I thought , man, our bye week comes at a really good time.  We'll have two more away games, six of our first nine will come after that .   You know, we'll have a good reset after 10 games, wherever we are. And so it was. Now we'll go to Chris. Hi Todd, you always talk about being under construction. Are good teams perpetually , in a way, under construction because they're always looking to improve in areas where maybe, you know, they'll succeed? Oh, yes.   I mean , everything in life, right? I mean, right?  Whether it's any job , any relationship, right? What is your religious belief, right? You're always under construction.   You 're always trying to improve, aren't you? You always try to create the best version of yourself individually and then collectively as a group.   I mean , that's what you should be doing. And that's all we're going to continue doing as staff, as an organization, and as players.  I mean, I don't know any other way than to be continually self-aware, to look in the mirror and say, "How can we improve ?" And stay humble or they will humiliate you. That's how it is.  And keep looking for margins, advantages that you can take advantage of . That was kind of a repetition, but it's just in general, simply what you can keep doing to improve. And that's why when you get into forecasts or what's ahead, it's something we might talk about right outside the building, right? As for where we stand. But once we enter the building, it's all about that day. From the moment we meet at 8:00 in the morning, everything revolves around that day.  It's about what we're going to achieve that day, and that's what we control. Now, let's talk about Spencer. Hey Todd, you talked a little bit about, you know, feeling like the week off was a good time.   I know there's also a lot of talk about how coaches handle the bye week.   You know, Andy Reid is famous for giving his team a whole week off.   This is your first time doing this as head coach, what's your philosophy on it? I know Denzel tried to convince you to give them a week off, but how are you going to handle them? Well, he's convinced me twice now. He achieved it after I prepared the calendar;  He and Malik came to see me and flattered me.   I mean, they talked about my hat and my clothes, about how good I looked.   I mean , they went all out. And I gave them an extra day, you understand?  I was going to keep them here on Thursday and they asked if we could finish on Wednesday. So they appealed a little to my emotional side. And of course, they kept trying. If you ask the players, they think they'll probably be able to show up to play on Sunday, and they're totally wrong.  So I gave in.  I gave them the day off, okay?  They didn't come today, but we'll come tomorrow.  We will end the match.  We'll go over some things we were going to cover anyway, and then we'll practice on Wednesday.  It will be a short practice, but we will go out onto the field.  We will run and lift weights. And we have a lot of room for improvement.  There will be plenty of days off, okay? But there's a lot of room for improvement because our job is to make football work well. I want their bodies to be well. I want your minds to be ready for the next seven weeks, but our job is to make sure football runs smoothly. And then, when you rebuild an offensive line like you guys did in the offseason, there were always going to be, you know, some adjustment issues, plus you have two rookies in that group, obviously.   When you saw the replay, did you feel that yesterday's event was like the culmination of them finally understanding it? And how have you seen that group continue to improve, especially Spencer and Austin in their first season? In some aspects growth is noticeable , but in others it is not as fast as we would like, especially in the ground game in terms of our identifications, our awareness and teamwork. We had a couple of protection issues, but I think our guys have worked really hard and been diligent in correcting the things we can improve.   They allow us to train them and continue understanding where we want to go, so I've been very impressed by their willingness to work. Now we just need to play in a much cleaner way, not only in the front line, but in all areas, so we can string together better plays and get going faster. Now let's talk about Cam. Hi Todd, I wanted to ask you a specific question about one of your players, Malachi Corley.   We 've seen him be very productive for you on special teams and yesterday he had even more production on offense. After the game he spoke about how grateful he was for the opportunity and for simply being there for his team What can you say about what you've seen from Malachi, both in special teams and when he's used offensively And how does that affect other guys in different positions who are in those special teams roles, waiting for their moment, staying ready for when you call them? Well, you're always looking for a player's elite trait and what they can contribute to help you move the ball on offense, defense, or special teams, and he's a physical player who brings that to the offense.  So I think you can design plays around that, running the ball, with pass action plays or naked plays ;  We've done a good job with him in the last few weeks and this week it just worked. As we always say, the ball finds the energy and the ball finds the guys who work hard. And he's one of those guys.  And that is to his credit. He has continued working, he comes to practice every day with a smile on his face and he loves being a Cleveland Brown. Let's go with Ashley. Hey Todd, I have a question after you've reviewed the video, because I know you were asked about the defense and the way Rudy was sending, uh, the blitzes yesterday, but after reviewing it, uh, what did you think of the job those guys did and again of the job Rudy did in running the game that way? Well, I think they did a great job staying aggressive, and I think that's the most important thing. You know, it's difficult to manage a match. Until you do it, it's difficult when things don't go the way you want.   It feels so hard to find a move that works, and it's, it's, it's that you're a little more hesitant. Or when they're scoring, you're trying to grab onto something;  You think they're play calls, and in part they are, and in part they're execution And when things are going your way and you have the momentum, it seems like you can choose any move and hell, just pick one and it will work or you're going to pick a blitz and there's some truth to that. And I thought they did a great job by staying that way. You know, it was working, maintaining, being aggressive, it forced them to execute And that's the most important thing, and I think it wasn't just Rudy, but the staff in terms of, uh, training him and getting it executed. And it was the same on offense.  I mean, how are we going to stay aggressive?  It's easy to be aggressive when you know you're going to be good and get back on track and you're converting third chances because you're not afraid to throw the ball into the field on the first down. When you're not very good at converting third chances and you're not very good at getting back on track, you're going to have a lot of "three and outs," especially if you're making attempts on first chances.  So it just becomes much easier, the flow is much simpler.  And I thought our personnel, especially in defense, did a great job of Along with Tony and Joe.  Let's start with you , Tony. Um. So, Todd, the bye week not only gives you guys the opportunity to self-analyze the training operation, but the entire football operation in general.   It gives them the opportunity to perhaps have conversations with Andrew Berry that they wouldn't have if there were a game coming up soon So, with that in mind, I want to ask you, have you and Andrew had a discussion about Watson's future beyond this year? Uh, we haven't had it.   Do you think this is a good time to start with that? Hmm.  Don't know.  You'll have to ask Andrew that.  I, I, I really don't think that far ahead.  Not really.   I 'm really not in a position to talk about any of our players. We still have six or seven games left Lots of American football to play.   I'm only worried about what we're going to review in tomorrow's training and the corrections. I'm concerned about Wednesday, what situations we want to work on with the lightweight team, and then think about the Raiders. And there will be plenty of time.  I'm sure that's what Andrew and his department do. But ultimately, our job is to prepare the team as best as possible each week to give our best and win games.  And that's a question for Andrew. But we haven't really had discussions ; most of our staff haven't talked about moving forward.   Alright .  Thank you. We finished with Joe. Two quick ones and they are somewhat related. How much research can they do during the bye week on getting better starts, and did the game really start with 15 minutes left in the first quarter and not at the start of the second? Yes, Joe.  Don't know.  I've been analyzing it.  It's not something we don't review over the weeks, nor that we don't analyze ourselves or what we ask for, but obviously what we're doing isn't working. So that's obvious.  I mean, we have to do something different. We tried to be more aggressive yesterday and still got away in three plays, so we'll keep trying because that can easily change.   Just like the back can change .  All we can do is observe what we are doing.  We're not going to change players.  We're not going to change the plan. So we need to figure out what we 're doing wrong, whether it's in the warm-up, or how to get a quick start, which is what we're asking for, but we certainly need to work to fix it. And you've had a lot of crazy games this year. What was that? What term was that? You've had a lot of wacky or crazy games. There you have it.  Alright. Where does yesterday's game stand, having been down 17-0 and managing to come back, and how did that second half unfold? Well, I mean, I thought the fact that the Ravens were down 10-0 was something, then the Titans were down 14-0, and then you get to 17-0, and nothing on this team surprises me because of the character we have, how hard they work, and the connection they have. Um, it's not a sustainable position to be in, as we all know.   I mean , that's not it, but it's a credit to our players and, no matter what it takes, you know, they got off to a fast start, right? So they're trying to figure out how to end it, right?  Hey, what a great start, right?  And then it's like, well, they didn't finish and we didn't get off to a fast start, and our guys struggled to regain momentum. And we came close in Pittsburgh. You know, when the score was 13-6 and we could have scored a touchdown there, man.  Let's just stop them before halftime.  Just knock them down in that run and who knows, it's 13-6.   We simply didn't do it at that time And that was the difference in that game.  In this game it was the field goal, then the save, and then the great play.  So we certainly need to do a better job starting fast and giving ourselves a chance to stay within striking distance, because I love the way our guys play at the end. And that is, again, a credit to our boys, but we certainly need to start faster.

title: Von Miller Talks 49ers Game| Player Interviews
text: you know that that play um we were in zero blitz and you know I had Christian McCaffrey to the flat and you know it's easy for people to be like man you got to be a pet the car why you 37 year old mom man I I rush the passer I rush the passer I play around but I think what's a what's a lowkey or not even low-key one of the things that I do really well is is you pass coverage. Um, I'm good in coverage. I never get the ball thrown to me because I'm always on my guard. I'm always doing what I'm what I'm what I'm supposed to do. I always have tight coverage. If we go back to the week before, you know, versus the Colts, I had Jonathan Taylor in the Flats. I had him appeal the same type of, you know, responsibility. So, do you want to be covering Christian McCaffrey every play of the game? No. Well, in those situations, for us to be the type of defense that we want to be, to be a championship style defense, those are plays that I'mma be I'mma have to make. Um, at the very least, at least scratch them on or trip them up or survive the down. Um, I could have played that better and it had nothing to do with with speed or quickness. I just was too fast to get outside. I had to I had the sideline to my left. If I can slow play it and be on the inside of his hip, you know, does he does he still catch it? So, he ran a he ran an angle route cuz I I mean, I jumped outside and I gave him the angle route. But, as a defensive coordinator in that situation, you want to be aggressive. We're trying to win the game. We we we had an opportunity to um create momentum. We were down by six points. If we could just get off the field, it was it was second and nine. And as a defensive coordinator, you want to be aggressive. You want to win the game. If it was the other way around and we were playing some conservative defense and they ran all the time out, then they'd be saying, "Why why we went aggressive?" Me as me as a 16-ear vet and I aspire to be, you know, a GM one day, team president one day. That's the type of mindset that I want in those type of games. So, do you pass the hard down around? I could have played um better technique. Does he still does he still catch it? Maybe it's it's Christian McCaffrey, but I believe in my ability to be able to make that play and at the very least pass interference, holding, just be able to survive it down. >> So, you were anticipating him going to the flat. Yeah. >> And outside he go inside. >> I had a pee. So, I was anticipating him running like a flare route to the sideline and I, you know, I overthought it. you know, my watched too much film and I jumped outside thinking he was gonna, you know, cross my face and he end up cutting right back inside and I should have just kept my eyes on him, but I looked back at the quarterback and by the time I looked back at Christian McCaffy, he had the ball and it was off to the races. >> On a play like that, do you need the Bliss to get there, make it get there? >> Well, Bliss can't get there if I don't cover if if he if he if he wins so fast. So, >> that was that was on me. And you know, I believe everything in life happened for a reason. I'm best suited for the success on the football field if I'm able to make that play and the failure from that play. I got so much confidence in myself and my game. This is my 16th year in the NFL. I've had tough plays like that before. I've had great plays like that before. I'm the one that is best suited to to wear that jacket of adversity and be a, you know, a model for my guys. This is how you handle it. I'm not about to put that on coach or put that on another player. I have to be better and I can be better. It's not it's not a a pipe dream saying that I can slow down Christian McCaffrey in that moment where we need to make a play. I have 100% confidence in myself and I can do it. I just got to find a way to make it happen. If you look at that play, all I had to do is just be a little bit more patient on the inside. Like I said, does he out Does he out run me? Yeah, probably. I had been coached on how to play um that that route. I've had examples of that route. Went over that play in practice this week. I was more than prepared. But for some reason, I didn't make the play. That had nothing to do with with Christian Parker. You know, that was me. And you want, like I said, we playing the 49ers. We down by six points. You want to be aggressive to try to make a play credit turnover. And all I got to do is guard them for two seconds. It's not like I'm guarding them for for 10 seconds down the field. like I I I needed to guard him for two seconds. I was too quick outside. He beat me within one second. I didn't even I I couldn't guard him enough to have the blitz hit there. So, that had nothing to do with Christian Parker. It's on me as a player. And that it's not like that's an exotic play. Defenses around the NFL run that exact same play. Zero blitz, outside guys peel. And I would implore I would say, you know, it's probably half of the teams in the NFL where I can still cover better than any outside linebacker defensive end. It's just tough situation going against Chris McAffrey and I could have been a little bit more patient to, you know, guard him a little bit longer. >> What do you say to people say you go in the Hall of Fame because you're a pass rusher, not because you cover running back? See if if I'm going y'all not really y'all don't know y'all history on me. Do y'all remember that play in Super Bowl 50 versus Cotry. I got picks on guys now. Do I want to run Champ Bailey? No. But I I definitely have that in my bag. And it's not like I haven't shown that in practice. It's not like I they just threw me under. Like I've shown examples on I've I've played that that route in practice. I've played that route in games. Week before had Jonathan Taylor on the wheel route. Um I'm the guy for the job. And I always say, you know, I'm I'm best suited out of all the outside linebackers in that room, whether it's RG, um, James Houston, Easy, Malachi, I'm the guy for the job. I 16 years in the NFL, I know coverages, I know routes. I was just too quick on getting out there. That had nothing to do with Christian Parker or the play call. >> You say that, you says that microcosm of the season has happened, not you, but with different guys. >> Yeah. And I'm I'm the model of the show. like this is how you this is how you do it. You don't to be a championship style defense, to be an elite player, you don't try to push that off on somebody else. You take ownership in it. You wear that jacket. >> And I'm and I'm the perfect model for it. >> Right. I'm just saying when it's a my crowd season happen not with you all the time with other guys, >> then that falls on who. If it if it keeps happening and the same thing keeps happening, >> is it a communication issue? Is it what just execution issue? How what do you how do you how does that not fall on the leadership? >> You know, I'm 37 years old and I tell you what, these >> these young players, they crazy, man. [laughter] They crazy, man. I don't want to put it on the players, man. But hey, it's not just us, man. It's around the league, man. These young dudes, they crazy, man. They crazy, man. We got great teachers on this team, man. Whether it's, you know, I I can appreciate great teaching and great coaches, and I've been around a lot of great coaches. Christian Parker is a genius. Um he's a great coach. Um you know the schemes that he has for us, you know, we just not bringing it to life. I got a I got faith in Christian Parker, faith in Coach Ch, the MD defensive line coach Brandon, you know, BT Jordan, you know, all our guys from inside linebackers, the quarterbacks. We got guys that are suited for the job. It's just, you know, on SS players. The way I played that had nothing to do with the call. I was too anxious to get outside. I knew the route and I was just trying to cut him off and ended up coming inside. That had nothing to do with, you know, coach Chid or coach Christian Parker. I was more than prepared, more than ready to go. It was a it was a great aggressive play call in a time where we really needed to make a play. So, um I rather it be on me than anybody else and that's just that's just how I'm built. >> As a long time as a longtime vet, what kind of role do you think you play in trying to keep this defense together and and kind of get the ship turning? I I think um just being a model for it like I think you know Von Miller Christian McCaffrey and then the way I wear that jacket I think you know all my guys are watching me to see how I react when I came in here the same V happy joking um you know of course you know the mood could be it would be a whole lot better if we won but I'm a that's part of the reason why they brought me here too is to change the culture and be an example for these guys on how to be a championship style defense how to be an elite player the way you, you know, walk around the facility and the things that you do and the way you carry yourself and I would rather be me getting six sacks in the game, but the way you handle adversity, you know, really speaks louder than the way you handle success. >> Thanks, guys. Appreciate.

title: LIVE: The Houston Texans address the media
text: go about attacking today. >> I'm sorry. >> How do you guys go about attacking today with you had a football game in a couple days and you also >> Yeah. to review what just happened Sunday? >> Yeah, most definitely. Just moving forward. Moving forward, you know, watching the corrections first just about starting saying like we got to do a better job of being more disciplined. I think that's the biggest thing. We had too way too many penalties, myself included. You know, we're ball key. I got to watch the ball. Um, just cutting down on the penalties, man. Looking yourself in the mirror, man, and taking ownership of, you know, the things you didn't do right in this game, but also noticing the things you did do right in this game and taking that and using that momentum going into the Thursday night. >> He has to do a better job of coaching you [snorts] guys up. What does that mean, you know, 10 weeks into the season? Where's the disconnect and the miscommunication between the coaches and the players? Yeah, I mean I think it's just the execution, you know what I'm saying? Like I think they do a good job of, you know, presenting what, you know, we have to go out and do. And I think for us is just being in those live moments and being able to take a deep breath and, you know, do your job. I think that's just been the biggest thing right now is, you know, get the call, play the call, no matter how it may look. So you talk about disconnect and execution, man. It's just go out and execute, you know. Um, it's the same thing every week and it's things just not going our way like we wanted to. Um, and we just have to continue to rally, stand 10 toes down, continue to play ball, continue to have fun doing it, continue to bring the energy into the building, keep everybody uplifted, and keep this thing rolling. >> For the guys that's been here over the last three seasons, this is the first time that you all have really been in a position to where you won't you may not make the the postseason for the first time in your career. What is that like for you all as collective group that it may be the first time you may not make it? >> Yeah, it's different. Um, we want to stay optimistic and, you know, keep things on the positive side. Um, like I said, focusing on Thursday, getting that dub, getting that win, and continue to stay on this win column that we can. Um, but it has been different. It has been challenging. Um, especially like for some of the guys that have never really part been a part of losing before. But that's the challenge of the NFL. That's the challenge of football. Every year is going to be different. I say it all the time. And it's just a the matter of time and how you go about getting over this hump. And like I said, we have to keep, you know, coming in here with great energy, keep the morale up. Everybody keep doing their part and just finding a way to possibly win these games. >> Well, when you talk about the energy, [clears throat] are you, if you could just kind of explain to me, are you more so talking about guys who uh are maybe like losing confidence in those in those situations or what do you mean when you when you >> So, I say two things. I think we talk about energy just as far as first off I feel like going into the game everybody's always have great energy. Um I think practice the energy is great. I think we could take that energy from practice and come to Sunday. It was crazy cuz I was just telling Henry it's like um just about not how you play but you know you make a mistake in practice and it's like oh we can move on and then you get to the game and you make a mistake and it's like ah. So, like even for me, like being able to move on from that mistake and keeping that energy where it was at when you first got to the game or you're in the sequence of the game and realizing that one mistake doesn't define the whole game that you've played. Um, so we just talk about two types of energy. I think on the sideline you see everybody cheering, you know, seeing guys make plays, you know, cheering the offense on when they come off the field dapping them up. But it's the energy that happens when explosive happens. is the energy that happens when somebody makes a bad play or somebody make a mistake that we have to continue to keep the up morale on the team and make sure that the leaders including myself like I said last night um that we have to do a better job of making sure that that energy stays right. >> What did Cleveland do well down yesterday? >> Um man uh we watched Deshan Watson on tape and he was most definitely sitting in the pocket a little bit at eight yards. I thought yesterday he was more 10 to 12 yards. um some chips and stuff like that, but I feel like up front, you know, we got to the quarterback as much as we could. They chipped a lot. They kept the running backs in a lot. Deshawn scrambled a little bit. We can do a better job there. Um but it's always room for improvement. Have to be able to get off blocks a little bit faster, probably get our hands up on some of the short uh passes that he had um and just execute better. >> You talked about um being more disciplined and and eliminating the penalties. when those same issues um continue to show up. How do you how do you actually correct those? >> Yeah, it's in-house thing. You know what I'm saying? I think being a man, you have to look yourself in the mirror and know that, man. I think like the coaches, they do a really good job of, you know, discipline us and saying like what it is and what it's not. And I think for us as players that we have to be able to have that mental capacity and that mental focus to go out on the field and go through all the things that we've been through all week. You know, they they hit us with hard counts throughout the week. uh different, you know, calls that we may have gotten, no holding, stuff like that. Like we see all those things throughout the week and we have to do a better job of bringing that into the game Sunday. >> Earlier today, you' said as a defense, would you still have to go out there and execute the calls no matter what it may look like? Do you mean there's any lack of confidence or trust in what the call is or do you mean something else by that? >> No, I'm just saying like whatever the play that's getting called, go execute it. No matter what he called, no matter what it may look like, just go execute the call. Like whatever it looks like, like just go play the call. So I think that's the thing I think you know it's been a different year I will say that um you know confidence is up and down but that's with anything that you do whether you work whatever job you work at situations happen where sometimes you're not as confident as you want to be and I think like I said we have to do a better job as leaders making sure that everybody remains confident their ability if you have a good game bad game okay game like you know who you are at the end of the day one game doesn't define you a season doesn't define you a loss or win doesn't define you have to know who you are as an individual as that person. And so I look at this team and I look at a bunch of guys that we know who we are, but we have to continue to keep fighting for who we are and show up every day the men that we know we are and be able to go out and do our jobs that we know we can do. >> There's a theme throughout the season in particular yesterday that the second half the other team has some success against you guys. what's happening that are they attacking you differently and you guys just stay in what you do and try to execute it as well as you want or how like what is allowing that? >> Yeah, and it's crazy yesterday I mean we could talk about the beginning of the season and on so forth but yesterday man I I I thought we came out with great energy. Um, we got a three and out when defense hit the field. Um, got an interception. You know, they made some pivotal plays in the game. But if you go back and look at that game, it was neck and neck and we, it's one or two plays and we're in our own way again. We gave up two big explosives. It was nothing they did. It was all us. So that's what I'm saying. It's like teams are going to do the same thing as us. We gave up two big explosives. I mean, we can't do that. We have to get home. They max protect. We have to find a way up front to get off box and get home. have to do a better job of covering in the back end. So, it's all of us staying connected and, you know, doing our jobs, but like I said, we're in our own way. And I think that's the most frustrating part about it is because we see what's on tape. You know, they're not really changing up and doing anything special. They're just catching us lacking when we're not executing the best that we can. >> Do you feel like y'all are doing the same thing too? Because if they're doing the same thing and they're having success, does it feel like y'all are making any adjustments? Yeah, but their success is not based on, I would say, a lack of scheme. It's just one person is out of place or we're not getting home up front or we're not rushing like we need to up front. We're getting stuck on blocks. So, again, it comes back to us doing our job to the best of our ability. >> That's what I want to ask you. Over the last two seasons, y'all have had a top five defense, one defense last season. coming into this season, do you feel like maybe some of the offensive coordinators studied you all those last, you know, the last two years of film and made the adjustments that they needed to to find maybe some weaknesses in the defense? >> Yeah, most definitely. That's what the league is. You know, every year you're looking to get better offensively and defensively and we have a really great defense and you know, teams are going to study us, teams are going to play us differently. Um, and we just have to be prepared for that. But again, I think we look at most situations and most, >> you know, plays that's being played and coach puts the film up. Yeah. Sometimes it's going to be schematics. It's the league. They're going to drop a good play. Hey, we got you right there. But sometimes we're watching the film and it's just one person is out of place or up front we're not holding the gap or we're not setting the edge or we're not being stout and they're taking advantage of that. And so that's what I'm I'm trying to say. It's just like we can't continue to beat ourselves. You know, sometimes they are going to make good plays. You know, this is the NFL. It's going to be a great one-on-one matchup and either you're going to win or you're going to lose because that's what the league is. But most of the time we're beating ourselves because we're not in the place that we need to be in to stop the play. >> That's what Demo means by I need to coach him up better. >> Yes, sir. >> Well, I don't want to put words in your mouth, but it sounds like you're saying you guys believe in the defense. It's just things that you guys can control. >> Yeah, we just have to do a better job of executing. Just we we have to. And I really think we're a really great team. We're a really great defense when we just execute consistently. like we shut them out in the first half, we get to the second half, we give up again two big explosives and it's nothing that they did. It's all on us. We have to just be able to get home on some of these things and get off blocks and cover. >> Yeah, most definitely. I think he stepped up big time for us at the end of the day. A lot of teams still respect him as well, so they're going to chip him as well, but I thought our interior guys got off and did what they need to do inside. We put a lot of pressure up the middle. Um Logan had a hell of a day. Rank rushing inside had a hell of a day. And when then when Drock Drock made some pivotal plays for us getting to PBU. So um again go back to JD. I think he stepped in and filled that role really well. >> Talk about confidence being up and down this year. When was confidence at its highest? When was confidence at its lowest and where is it right now? >> Yeah, I think you just see it in different games. I think you see some games where the offense is really high and defense is probably low when the offense probably wasn't clicking and the defense was clicking and special teams. So I think just throughout the year you see the different games of where each different level of offense defense was very confident and sometimes we probably wasn't as confident. So just maintaining that level of confidence where everybody is high and everybody playing at a high level that's something that we can most definitely work on. At >> what point does the standard kind of change? Because we keep talking about standard and feels like kind of holding on to 2025 but it feels like this is a big enough sample size to where this is kind of what this defense is. At what point does that standard have like an expiration date? >> Yeah, the standard will never have an expiration date. What we've built here, what we have accomplished here, and what do the Miko has instilled here, that's going to always be. It's always going to be sworn. The mentality is not going to change because of what the outside people may say. We know what we built here. We know the type of people that we have in the locker room. What people want us to be is always going to be not going to match what we want to be. Our standards are always going to be higher than the outside noise wants us to be. And it doesn't feel good. It's frustrating. And obviously, you know, we're not in a position that we want to be in, but we're not going to waver. We're not going to change anything for anybody. Thank you. Good afternoon. Whatever it is that was [clears throat] again would have done differently. How does that happen in the game? Yes, I saw him when I was running past him. Yes, it was pretty obvious from the start. Yes. No, it was fine.  It was like, oh yeah. Tell us, you know, a football theory question here. You guys have been playing a lot of eight-man defenses the last three weeks: New England, Detroit , Indy. The opportunity to go above, I mean, seems simple enough, but what does that entail?  I mean, the receiver has to be open, you have to have communication.  I guess it's different with Kyle and with Malik, right?   You don't have that much communication with Kyle. Take us through those opportunities .  I mean, is it as simple as, yes, let's go deep, or what has to work there? Uh, I mean, it's really about doing your part.  The offensive line has to hold up for us.  Kyle needs to make a good pass. Omar League tiene que lanzar un buen balón y los receptores deben despegar desde la línea ante todo, correr una buena ruta, hacer un buen trabajo de arranque y salir con velocidad para ganar la ruta. As I said, I think that influences everything related to overcoming the defender in depth, especially when they know that's what we want to do. And we also need to implement the ground game.  He's running really well right now , so the deep-lying guys need to come up and slow him down or he's going to destroy them. So everything goes hand in hand;  When those opportunities to throw a long pass arise, we have to take full advantage of them because we won't have many. A two-part question.  How close is this team to winning? And the second part is that obviously this team has been losing by very, very narrow margins. But how do you balance seeing the progress and growth of many young people with the ultimate goal of wanting to win? I think we're close, and the recordings show that every week we're just one or two plays away from making a big difference in the game. Y creo que no hay que enfocarse en el pasado ni en el futuro, sino estar en el momento presente, ya sea analizando los videos hoy para ver qué podemos mejorar para la próxima semana, o salir el miércoles a tener un gran entrenamiento y ser consistentes;  I think that's it. I'm sure everyone has heard it: day by day nothing changes, but when you look back, everything is different.  I think that's what we're experiencing now, and at some point we'll look back and say, "Wow, this is where it all started." But right now we are in the middle of the process.  We're in the storm and we just have to keep going, keep swimming. And you know, everything will turn out as we want. Tell me about your process for getting ready because, you know, you've been inactive for a few games.  How do you stay ready for that moment? Uh, it's difficult.  Obviously, as a competitor you want to play every single match.  You want to be an important part of the success that's happening and make plays, but with that, as I said , comes the challenge of assuming your role.  And right now, my role is whatever it is. And whether they call me or not, I'm ready . I train every day as if I were going to play.   I never thought for a second that I wouldn't play.  I go out to train and I put in a lot of effort every week.  I help the guys when they ask for it and tell them what I see and what I think we can do to improve as a unit and as an offense.  And obviously, when the opportunity arises , I go out and try to make the most of it.  I always tell Barry that you can't complain about the cards you were dealt.  If you do that, you'll never win.  So you play the hand you were dealt, you keep going, and eventually you'll win.   I'm just continuing to prepare myself, going out to glorify God on the platform that gave me the opportunity. And when he gives me the opportunity to go out and make a play, I do it for him Jaylen, I know your touchdown came from a pass by Malik Washington, right?  But how would you evaluate Kyle McCord's first NFL start, based on what you saw of him? Yes, I'm very proud of him. Obviously, being the substitute, we talked a lot and spent a lot of time together too.  I know he was ready for that opportunity and he did great.  He was very calm during the meeting.  He controlled the team very well. He took command of us.  After each series he would come, walk with us and talk;  If he felt that something was his fault, he would say, "Hey, I owe you one."  And that's important for a quarterback coming in like that. And knowing that we all supported him, I think it gave him an extra boost of confidence .  And I said we were excited to go out and play with him and that he did some really good things.  And I hate that we couldn't finish it for him and get him his first win in his first start, but I'm sure he'll get one soon. Jaylen, based on that, you know, it's often said of a team that the biggest improvement made in a season is between weeks one and two What about Kyle between his first two starts?  In other words, what would you expect to be best for him in his second start? Uh, I think a lot of things, you know, I think the most important thing for him is that his confidence continues to grow.  Obviously, when you first go out there, there are many things happening at the same time .  There are many different movements and many different keys.  You're playing with many different teammates.  I mean, how many times has he actually thrown the ball to Malik Washington and Caleb? So, just familiarize yourself with them;  He made some very important pitches to Caleb yesterday and I think, you know, that will continue to grow and, like I said, we all trust him.   We 're all out there with him.  We're going through this with him, and I think that also gives him confidence.  Y creo que tendrá una sensación diferente al entrar esta semana, sabiendo a lo que se enfrenta y en qué puede hacer ajustes, mejorar, y qué podemos hacer nosotros también para ayudarlo mientras estamos ahí fuera. And a question about Buffalo, I know you haven't been here for years and years, but Buffalo has beaten the Dolphins in seven of the last nine games.   Is that all in the past?  This is a new team and I know it's a new year.   Does any of that remain in this team or is it simply a new year, a different game?   Do you know what I mean? Does that carry over into the present? I think it definitely carries over into the locker room with the players, and I'm sure some players have a different kind of hatred, I guess you could say, towards them. But I think that, in general, the message from the team and the coach is that we shouldn't worry so much about the opponent as about what we are doing. You know, we can defeat ourselves .  We truly believe that no one can beat us.  Simplemente nos ganamos a nosotros mismos, así que, si salimos a jugar con fuerza, con intensidad, a nuestro estilo, quiero decir, podemos mantenerlo, ya sabes, como queramos y salir con la victoria si jugamos de la forma correcta;  I think, as I said, we've demonstrated that every week in the video.  It was just a handful of plays that we let slip by or that, uh, we failed to convert, and that could have changed the course of the game. I think it's the same case for this week, whether it's against Buffalo or whoever;  So I think we'll just focus on ourselves, on what we can control, on what we can do to improve and take a step forward next week.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Recaps Week 10, Gives Updates On Injuries | Seattle Seahawks
text: Welcome everyone. Uh Bob, you want to get us started? >> It sounds like we have coach. >> Um yeah, sure. Uh hey Mike. It's also one of those things where like you can it's kind of like the outcome thing. You can say you want to tackle better, but what are the things you're doing to make that happen? So for for for me I think our focus is how we can become more decisive to start games uh really in all three phases to be able to you know put some leads together earlier in games. Uh I think you still feel our our our halfbacks taking another step in terms of building that chemistry between how things are blocked and where they're going to hit certain type of runs. So, uh that was good. Now, there there's still some there's still some things where we're going to talk as a staff and where we want to go back and and improve. And we'll I think we'll, you know, we'll take a step back here and and kind of reook at the adjustments we made after the uh after the Denver game and re-evaluate those things and have a plan of attack moving forward. But, uh definitely feel like there's more room to grow, which is exciting. You know, I think if you're running for over a hundred or whatever we whatever we did and feel like you can be better, I think that's a good place to be in. >> All right, that's it. title: The DiCecco Daily: What Recent Eagles Transactions Should Mean Going Forward
text: Hello everyone, what's new?  Welcome to another episode of The Check Own Daily. With you is Andrew De Cheek Own, Inside the Birds.com's Eagles reporter, and I look forward to continuing to kick off the second half of the season with the same enthusiasm.   The Eagles will be speaking to the media this week in preparation for their game against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and Monday brought a few roster changes, a whole slew of moves, actually. Tight end Zach Ertz and offensive tackle John Williams Jock were signed to the 53-player starting lineup. The Eagles also opened a practice window for running back Will Shipley, and additionally signed running back Jaden Blue, linebacker Chance Campbell and tight end Hayden Rucci to the practice squad, while releasing defensive back Sean Wade. So let's get through this, and at the end of the podcast I'll mention one small change in the coaching staff. So, signed to the main roster: Zach Ertz and Jonah Joku. Zach Ertz is eight receptions short of breaking Harold Carmichael's record for most receptions in franchise history.   He has 589, and Zach Ertz has 582.  Do I think this is the main reason for signing Ertz to the starting lineup?  No, but he is a seasoned veteran. He's been on the practice squad, it seems , since Week 3, the game against the Chicago Bears, for which he was drafted. And in such a poor season, why not bring back to the starting lineup a man who has done so much for the franchise and was one of the best, if not the best, tight ends in team history to enhance his legacy? But now the Eagles have five tight ends on the 53-man roster. So you have to think like that.  Dallas Godert is your starting player.  You're not going to take Ertz out of the lineup, otherwise why sign him to the first team?  Eli Stowers, a second-round pick, should get more playing time at the end of the season, and frankly , he deserves it. It seems the Eagles value Grant Calcaterra so much that they not only activated him from injured reserve a few weeks ago, but are also bringing him into the offense. So that leaves Johnny Munt.  Johnny Munt is an experienced 31-year-old player. He was signed as a free agent, counting on him to be a solid blocker.  We haven't really seen that this season.  To be honest, I think his playing time figures are too high compared to the performance he shows on the field.  And when you look at the other players I mentioned and Johnny Mant, I understand he has a good relationship with Sean Mannion and all that, but when you look at the moves the Eagles have made with Hollywood Brown and Fred Johnson, I think that could be a harbinger of a possible parting ways with Johnny Mant.   It's hard for me to imagine the Eagles keeping five tight ends on a 53-man roster for long.  Of course, at one time they had four quarterbacks, and that was a little unusual.  And this is also the same team that had seven defensive tackles on its 53-man roster in 2023. So there is no clear plan to rely on here.  But you have to look at the long term.   Will Johnny Mant be part of your future?  Will he be factored into the Eagles' long-term equation?  No, it won't .  And is he someone they could release and move to the practice squad if they want to keep him? Of course. So that's what makes me a little wary of what's going to happen at that position, and I think Johnny Munt will be redundant, but we'll have to wait and see how it all plays out, but that's my opinion, and you just have to look at players like Zach Ertz, Dallas Godert, Eli Stowers and Grant Calcaterra. Say what you want, but it seems like the team rates him higher than the public. He can also help on special teams, something Johnny Munth didn't really do.  So all these things should be taken into account. Jonah Williams—he's someone I added to my article this morning on insidethebirds.com as a young player who could get more playing time down the stretch. And Jonah Williams is someone who was with the Eagles in the spring and summer.  He played as a right and left winger.  I think he even worked a little part-time as a guard, maybe in the spring.  So it is very versatile.  He is more of a right-winger. He's 27 years old, signed as an undrafted free agent by the Tennessee Titans in 2023, and, it's worth adding, out of Boise State University.  What I can say about him is that he immediately caught my attention, as I kept seeing number 67 working with the second team back in the spring, and I took note of that.  Then we move on to training camp where he gets some serious game practice with the second squad, and to be honest, I didn't know much about him, so I started to look into his bio a little deeper.  He's a player who played in 16 NFL games, started nine times , and was called up from the practice squad once this year for the Eagles, but he didn't play in that game . But I was sure that the team was counting on him to some extent, given the number of playing moments he received in training camp with the second squad. These weren't just random workouts.
